question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 22 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 8 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(12, 22, 8) = 264 units.

Combined efficiency = (264 ÷ 12) + (264 ÷ 22) + (264 ÷ 8) = 22 + 12 + 33 = 67 units/hour.

Time taken = Total work ÷ Combined efficiency = 264 ÷ 67 = 3 ⁶³/₆₇ hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 ⁶³/₆₇ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A = 12 hours

Time taken by Pipe B = 22 hours

Time taken by Pipe C = 8 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 **Hours**

 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Pipe A

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Efficiency of Pipe A, Pipe B and Pipe C = 22 + 12 + 33 = 67 units/hour.

⇒ Time taken by them together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 264 ÷ 67 = 3 ⁶³/₆₇ hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 ⁶³/₆₇ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

If a pipe can fill a tank in 'x' hours, then the part of the tank filled in 1 hour is 1/x. The total work is simply considered as the LCM of all the individual times given.

Emptying Pipes

If an outlet pipe is connected that empties a full tank in 'y' hours, its efficiency is treated as a negative value. The part emptied in 1 hour becomes −1/y.

Combined Work Formula

If two filling pipes take 'a' and 'b' hours respectively to fill a tank separately, the total time taken to fill it together is calculated directly using (a × b) ÷ (a + b) hours.
